text:
maria: noticing a big drop in prefix cache hit-rate after the kernel bump late yesterday. sampled cohort hit-rate fell ~88% -> ~50%.

devon: ugh. exact deploy time?

maria: merged 1765320000, deployed 1765400000; spike appears 1765412000 on canary; attached request/keys show identical visible prompts mapping to different serialized keys.

maria: example snippet from logs:
```
request: {"system": "You are a helpful assistant", "messages": [...], "tools": [{"name":"search","args":{"q":"x"}}, {"name":"summarize","args":{}}]}
old_key (hit): prompt_v2|tokver:5|tools:search|summarize
new_key (miss): prompt_v2|tokver:5|tools:summarize|search
```

ajay: seems serializer changed field ordering; tool array no longer normalized.

lucy: tokenizer version the same? token counts?

maria: tokenizer pin still 5. token counts match. it's serialization ordering + minor system prompt whitespace normalization in the new kernel.

sam: quick mitigation: canonicalize tool names when generating cache keys (stable sort) and only include explicit order when route opts into order-sensitive semantics.

devon: agreed. implement deterministic tool-key canonicalizer and add a route-level flag to opt into order sensitivity.

ajay: warning: some users depend on tool order for behavior. removing order from key risks false positive cache hits -> behavior divergence.

lucy: proposal: default to sorted tool key, but include an optional header or flag e.g. "tool_order_strict":true to preserve order in the key when needed.

maria: runbook: (1) hotfix keygen to stable-sort tools -> push to canary (2) run a backfill worker to prepopulate recent normalized prefixes (3) monitor hit-rate and correctness.

devon: hotfix sketch:
```
def canonical_tool_key(tools, meta):
    names = [t['name'] for t in tools]
    if meta.get('tool_order_strict'):
        return '|'.join(names)
    return '|'.join(sorted(names))
```

sam: build a short-lived backfill task to replay N minutes of requests, compute normalized keys and prefill KV so clients see fewer cold misses.

infra-bot: scheduled job created: prefix-prefill-1765436200 -> starts in 35m

deploy-bot: canary deploy runtime-hotfix v3.2.1 -> 1765436300

maria: canary numbers (first 20m): hit-rate went 50% -> 79% on sampled sessions. still below baseline but much improved.

ajay: remaining gap likely from system prompt whitespace and unicode normalization differences.

lucy: recommend normalizer: trim, collapse consecutive spaces, unicode NFKC, remove ephemeral timestamps/uuids from system prompt before keying.

devon: add sanitizer pipeline before tokenization and document the canonicalization guarantees in the API contract.

maria: tests: unit tests for permutation stability + an integration replay of 1k recent sessions asserting hit delta < 5% vs baseline.

sam: rollout plan: canary (20 nodes) 1h, backfill worker, A/B 50% for 6h, full rollout if hit within 3% and no correctness regressions.

ajay: add route config toggle: "prefix_cache_order_sensitive": true/false. default false.

devon: PR queued: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/5421

maria: short-term for impacted customers: extend prefix TTL and enable per-route warmup for their routes.

sam: root cause: kernel serializer optimization made object field ordering stricter for perf; wins for determinism but broke our external key stability contract.

ajay: long-term: require serializer changes to run a key-stability report and replay harness before merge. create a contract test in CI.

maria: tracking ticket PERF-6234. will update once canary finishes. if we see sustained regressions after rollout, rollback v3.2 and open incident.

lucy: I'll open sanitizer PR with canonical examples and test vectors.

maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
